paragraphs.text: A DSH plugin that watches its own sessions, keeps what it learns, and changes the harness it runs in
— but only keeps a change a second run proves.
# dsh-fracture
A DSH plugin that reads your finished sessions, finds where the harness makes the agent fail, writes
the fix as data, and runs the task twice to check whether the fix helped.
English | 日本語
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two properties matter before reading the code:
- A candidate that ships a `plugin/` directory runs in a separate `dsh` process, so unverified code

never loads in the process that judges it.
- Candidates that touch approval, sandbox policy, the plu
gin manager, or this plugin are rejected before they are stored, and again before they are probed.
The reasoning behind the tier boundaries is in docs/仕組み.md (Japanese).
## What it is
DSH builds an agent out of an ordered list of plugin rows. A model, a prompt section, a skill root,
a tool, an approval policy: each is a row with its own config.
Two consequences follow. A harness is data, so a candidate harness is a diff against the current one
. And two harnesses can exist at the same time, so a change can be judged by running the same task o
n both instead of asking a model whether its own idea sounds good.
## The problem
Three failures are common in a setup that nobody has time to tune.
**The same mistake outlives the session.** A tool fails because the project uses pnpm, or because th
e fixture has to be built before the test runs. The model works it out, the session ends, and the ne
xt session starts from nothing.
**Harness tuning is guesswork.** Someone edits the system prompt, decides the agent feels better, an
d has no way to check. The edit stays. The next edit lands on top of it. Two months later nobody kno
ws which line matters.
**Nothing accumulates.** When a session goes well, the procedure that made it go well is not written
down anywhere the next session can read.
All three have the same cause: nothing in the loop records what happened, and nothing tests a change
against a baseline. Fracture adds both, and lets them run unattended.
## What it does
It records every finished turn as facts rather than prose: which tools ran, in which order, what fai
led, whether you had to step in and correct it. After twenty turns that log becomes a digest. After
three clean repetitions of one procedure, the procedure becomes a skill. The digest and the skill li
st go into the prompt as a short index, so the agent knows what it has learned without loading every
thing it has recorded.
It also changes the harness, but only where a measurement supports the change, and the depth of what
it may change on its own is bounded:
| Tier | What changes | Gate |

| Memory | observations, digest, journal | none, additive |
| Skills | `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`, reg

istered live | none, additive |
| Composition | prompt rows, skill-dir rows, tool toggles | probe ve

rdict plus a watch window, auto-revert on regression |
| Code | a candidate plugin module | **human*
*: `dsh plugin add` |
The first two tiers are knowledge. They cannot execute anything, cannot widen a permission, and are
removed by deleting a file, so they run without asking. The third is a data change the loop owns and
can undo, so it runs without asking but is watched for twelve turns afterwards and reverted if the
numbers get worse. The fourth decides what code runs inside your process, so the loop may author it
and probe it, and you decide whether it runs.
That last line is deliberate. An agent that can install its own code needs no human in the loop to d
o it, and its first bad change would then be the one change it cannot detect from the inside.
Everything it writes is a file you can read: `.dsh/fracture/`.
A distilled skill, an applied change, and a revert each post one collapsed notice into the session,
so the loop never acts silently. Nothing else does, because a notice per turn stops being informatio
the loop never acts silently. Nothing else does, because a notice per turn stops being information.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
That is the distribution path. It installs from the repository and builds the package on the way in.
pnpm refuses to run build scripts of a git-hosted package by default, so the first attempt fails wit
h `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`. Copy the `allowBuilds` line the error prints into `$DSH_HO
ME/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml` and run the command again. The key contains the fetched commit
hash, so it changes whenever main moves.
Restart once. No configuration is required: observation and memory start immediately.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Tools
The loop uses these internally, and any of them can be called by hand.
| Tool | What it does |
| `fracture_diagnose` | Ranks what the current harness does badly: tool failure rates, repeated read

s, denied approvals, compaction pressure, message feedback. |
| `fracture_propose` | Sends a propose

r subagent to write one candidate as `candidate.json` plus optional `skills/` or `plugin/`. |
| `fra
cture_probe` | Runs a task on the current harness and on the candidate, then compares. Writes `runs/

<id>/report.md`. |
| `fracture_plan` | Turn a request into checks that can be run or read |
| `fract
ure_adopt` | Turns a probed candidate into an installable bundle and appends the lesson. Never insta

lls. |
| `fracture_status` | What was learned, what was proposed, how each candidate scored. |
| `fr
acture_loop` | Runs diagnose → propose → probe → apply once, with the same gates the idle trigger us

es. |
| `memory_search` | Searches the digest, past turns, and distilled skills. |
## Documentation
| File | Contents |

| README.ja.md | The same introduction in Japanese |
| docs/仕組み.md | How it works: the four tiers, t

he triggers, the watch window, the protected surface |
| CONTRIBUTING.md | Development, release step

s, and what a good pull request looks like |
| SECURITY.md | What counts as a vulnerability and what

is design |
| CHANGELOG.md | What changed in each version |
The design and contribution documents are written in Japanese. That is a deliberate choice: they are
read by the person who maintains the loop, and a translated design document loses the precision tha
n who maintains the loop, and a translated design document loses the precision that makes it useful.
